newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: PARLIAMENT POSTPONES SAVINGS REFUND VOTE.
newsitem.headline: PARLIAMENT POSTPONES SAVINGS REFUND VOTE.

text.p: Lithuania's parliament on Thursday postponed a vote on a law refunding people who lost bank deposits during the inflation in the early years of independence and the chaos of the fall of the Soviet Union.
An estimated one million people lost deposits, meaning the government will have to pay out around 3.2 billion litas.
The reading of the law will now take place next Thursday, parliament's protocol office said.
The government has said that the repayments will be made from the receipts of privatisation and not from the budget.
Payments are due to begin next year and are expected to take around three years.
